clauses.reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12292, signed February 23, 1981 (46 FR 13967, issue of February 25, 1981), which recites the purpose "in order to conform existing Executive Orders to changes resulting from that Act" and whose section 10 states "Sec. 10. The following are hereby revoked:" with item (d) naming Executive Order No. 9932 of February 27, 1948 by number. Section 11 states "This Order shall be effective as of February 15,1981.", so the revocation is recorded as effective 1981-02-15, the stated effective-as-of day; the alternative reading is the signing date 1981-02-23. This clause is paragraph 1 (competitive status for Foreign Service Reserve officers reached for probational appointment): the grant of competitive status to a Government officer or employee assigned to the Foreign Service as a Reserve Officer who was serving under a war service indefinite or temporary indefinite appointment and is reached in regular order for probational appointment. It depends on this order alone and the revocation is of the whole order by number.

It depends on this order alone and the revocation is of the whole order by number. The substitution changes the named agency in this clause and does not end it.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (13 FR 1099, issue of March 2, 1948) is Executive Order 9932, Acquisition of Competitive Status and Reemployment of Certain Persons Appointed or Assigned to the Foreign Service, signed by Harry S. Truman at The White House, February 27, 1948. I read the whole order, which has seven numbered paragraphs; the representation is the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF and page images were not inspected. Inventory corrected: the machine list had eight clauses including a fragment consisting of the token 1946, which is the tail of paragraph 2; the corrected list has seven clauses, one per numbered paragraph. End: express revocation by Executive Order 12292 (1981). The dossier chain also lists Executive Order 9452 of 1944, which predates this order and appears only because the held record under that number is the 1981 Federal Register page range that contains Executive Order 12292. Executive Order 12107 (1979) is a later amendment of the agency name in paragraph 6, recorded as a later event.

A held Federal Register text filed under number 9970 contains a Civil Service Commission regulation that cites this order and is not a revocation or amendment. The held texts citing this order's number are Executive Order 12292, copies of its 1981 pages, Executive Order 12107 and that regulation; none other revokes or supersedes it before 1981.","independent_command_check":"Paragraph 6 delegates rulemaking to the Civil Service Commission, but it is part of this order's text and is not a continuing standing rule outside the order; the substitution by Executive Order 12107 changed the named agency without ending the delegation. Statutes cited as authority are separate sources of law and are not claimed to have ended.","savings_check":"Executive Order 12292 contains no saving or transition provision in its held text; no residual effect of this order is shown to depend on its continued force.
